display.title: Episode 116: Life in the Hands of the Tongue, Chapter 2 (Adar II)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi's show for the second day of Adar II: practicing with groggers, Shema with two sisters, and the end of the story of the hunter, the lion's milk and the boastful tongue.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on the second day of Adar II 5744. Uncle Yossi gets everyone ready for Purim, practicing with groggers and the joy of Adar, and the Hakochainik march is played with groggers too. After the sponsor, he recaps last week's chapter: a hunter brought a gravely ill king a bucket of lion's milk, and in a dream every part of his body argued over who deserved the reward until the tongue claimed to be king. Before story time, two sisters recite the Shema, and Uncle Yossi links saying it together to the achdus of Purim. He explains that the story comes from Tz'enah U'r'enah and is told in honor of the Chofetz Chaim's 50th yahrzeit and the worldwide campaign for guarding one's speech. In the conclusion, one wrong word lands the hunter in prison, and one right word saves him and cures the king. Uncle Yossi ends with Shlomo HaMelech's teaching that death and life are in the hand of the tongue. The show closes with ads, a Moshiach Times report from Brazil, and the yahrzeit of Uncle Yossi's mother.
display.lesson: Death and life are in the power of the tongue: guard your speech and use your tongue for brachos, davening and words of Torah.
